summary.text: Philip A. Palmesano is the incumbent Republican and Conservative Party candidate for New York State Assembly District 132 in the November 3, 2026 general election.
First elected to the Assembly in 2010, he was appointed Ranking Member of the Ways and Means Committee in February 2026.

paragraphs.text: Palmesano, known as Phil, was born and raised in Hornell, graduated from Hornell High School in 1987 and from St. Bonaventure University in 1991.
He worked for 15 years as a local aide to lawmakers including Assemblyman Donald Davidsen, Assemblyman Jim Bacalles, Congressman Randy Kuhl and state Senator George Winner.
In November 2009 he was elected to represent the City of Corning on the Steuben County Legislature, and he took office in the Assembly in January 2011.
Palmesano represents the 132nd Assembly District, which includes most of Steuben County, all of Schuyler and Yates counties, and portions of Chemung and Seneca counties.
He was Ranking Member of the Energy Committee for 13 years and Assistant Minority Leader from 2020 until 2026, and he also serves on the Rules Committee.

His official biography lists the business climate, tax and mandate relief, infrastructure, organ and tissue donation, and energy affordability and reliability among his priorities, and says he lives in Corning.
